gloss_hint: This means a disposition toward inelegance (means of communicating ideas), of a piece with inelegant, graceless and ungraceful, shown in stiffness, barbarism and cacophony; the opposite pole is elegance.
This means a disposition toward consent (special intersocial volition), of a piece with consenting and unconditional, shown in acquiescence, compliance and agreement.
This means a disposition toward chance (prospective volition), of a piece with unintentional, unintended and accidental, shown in luck, mascot and speculation; the opposite pole is intention.

This means a disposition toward prohibition (special intersocial volition), of a piece with prohibitive, prohibitory and restrictive, shown in inhibition, veto and disallowance; the opposite pole is permission.
This means a general tendency to feel threat and act from it (sympathetic affections), of a piece with threatening, menacing and abusive, shown in menace, abuse and intimidation.
This means a disposition toward repose (voluntary action), of a piece with reposing, relaxed and unstressed, shown in rest, relaxation and halt; the opposite pole is exertion.
This means a disposition toward willingness (volition in general), of a piece with willing, minded and fain, shown in heart, disposition and inclination; the opposite pole is unwillingness.
This means a disposition toward guilt (moral affections), of a piece with guilty, culpable and censurable, shown in guiltiness, culpability and criminality; the opposite pole is innocence.

This means a disposition toward desuetude (volition in general), of a piece with unaccustomed, unused and unwonted, shown in obsolescence, want of habit and want of practice; the opposite pole is habit.
This means a disposition toward taciturnity (means of communicating ideas), of a piece with silent, mute and mum, shown in silence, muteness and curtness; the opposite pole is loquacity.
This means a disposition toward refusal (special intersocial volition), of a piece with refusing, restive and recusant, shown in rejection, noncompliance and denial; the opposite pole is offer.

This means a disposition toward approbation (moral affections), of a piece with approving, commendatory and complimentary, shown in approval, sanction and advocacy; the opposite pole is disapprobation.

This means a disposition toward detraction (moral affections), of a piece with detracting, defamatory and derogatory, shown in disparagement, depreciation and vilification; the opposite pole is flattery.
This means a disposition toward demon (religious affections), of a piece with demonic, demonical and impish, shown in daemon, demonology and fiend; the opposite pole is jupiter.
